solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Approaching 40mph, losing power, I get tense and shirty with old pedestrian ultimately. That's all wrong

indicators.note: the setter declares everything before it is wrong, so the gathered letters must be rearranged
losing says a letter is dropped from the speed abbreviation

parts.note: mph is miles per hour
P is the physics symbol for power
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word pedestrian

explanation.surface: A speeding driver nearing forty mph loses their temper with a slow pedestrian, and the whole scene is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes P from MPH to leave MH; 'That's all wrong' then rearranges MH, I, GET, T, SHIRTY, O and N. The '40' looks like a speed, but it is an age.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in their thirties is nearing their fortieth birthday, the idiomatic label for that age group.

clue.text: Translated another 'ambient' European novel

indicators.note: translated means put into another form, so the letters are rendered in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone translated another 'ambient' European novel into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translated' rearranges ANOTHER, AMBIENT and E. The novel is Jerome K. Jerome's 1889 comic account of a Thames boating trip.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a famous comic book of fiction by Jerome K. Jerome.

clue.text: Beer and cig's bad for unemotional type

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of beer and cig are in a corrupted order

parts.note: cig is the word itself; the 's stands for 'is' and gives no letters

explanation.surface: Beer and cigarettes are bad for you, a health warning aimed at a cold person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges BEER and CIG. The 's is 'is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold, aloof person is informally called this, from the frozen floating mass of ice.

clue.text: Drop in rent

definitions.meaning: a drop of liquid from the eye when crying
a rip or split in fabric

explanation.surface: A fall in what a tenant pays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is not money here but a rip; the noun and verb are spelt alike but said differently.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a drop shed when weeping; the other is a rip, which is what a rent in cloth is.

clue.text: Liberated group starts to finance revolutionary European enterprise

parts.note: a set is a group of things belonging together

indicators.note: starts to points at the opening letter of each of the following four words

explanation.surface: A group was freed to fund a radical pan-European business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone is to release them, so liberated means released from captivity.

clue.text: Smell mounts after most of mud cakes

indicators.note: after puts the reversed smell behind the trimmed mud
most of means the word mud is used without its last letter
in a down clue, mounts means the word climbs, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a sniff is a smell or a quick inhalation

explanation.surface: A smell rises from the mud cakes, a picture of a dirty puddle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'mounts' means read upwards, so the smell word appears as FFINS; 'most of' and 'after' place it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small baked items of the bun or cake kind, eaten toasted in Britain.

clue.text: Private charity supports college

indicators.note: the phrase private charity holds the word inside it, carrying it across the break between the two words

explanation.surface: A privately funded charity backs a college.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Private' into 'charity'; 'supports' says the phrase holds them up.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical college, an institution for vocational and further education, is shortened to this informal name.

clue.text: Separate lives lead to troubled daughter leaving

parts.note: someone who lives is, i.e. exists

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order
leaving says a letter departs from the letters before they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Separating lives can upset a family when a daughter leaves home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lives' is the verb, not the plural noun. 'leaving' and 'troubled' together leave the letters OLATE once the D goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate something is to set it apart from others, the verb sense of cutting off.

clue.text: I.e. treating sorts out this bug

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters are disarranged

parts.note: the two letters of the abbreviation, used as they stand

explanation.surface: That is, a medical treatment sorts out this bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IE, TREATING and SORTS. 'sorts out' looks like a phrase, but 'out' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomach infection is often called a bug, and inflammation of stomach and intestines is such an illness.

clue.text: Construct again broken entrance removing name

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters are smashed and reassembled
removing says one letter is taken away from the doorway word first

explanation.surface: A broken doorway must be rebuilt after the nameplate is taken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' drops one N from ENTRANCE, and 'broken' rearranges ETRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out an event again is to rebuild it, as with a historical staging of a battle.

clue.text: Agents fine cast

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the cast of a play are its performers

explanation.surface: Talent agents praise a fine cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a business agent who buys and sells on commission, so the plural matches agents.

clue.text: Exact fraction of seventy

indicators.note: a fraction is a part, so the answer is a part of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A precise share of seventy, as in arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: An even sum is exact, with nothing left over, as in an even hundred.

clue.text: Female bird is weak

parts.note: a rail is a marsh bird, like the water rail

explanation.surface: A female bird is feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail and weak are synonyms for lacking physical strength.

clue.text: Scottish landowner fails to finish retreat

indicators.note: the landowner's title is left without its final letter

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish estate owner

explanation.surface: A Scottish laird fails to complete his retreat from the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to finish' cuts the last letter D from LAIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: A den or hideaway where an animal or villain withdraws is a retreat.

clue.text: Fanatical baron takes part in invasion

indicators.note: the baron joins in, so his letter goes inside the attack word

parts.note: a raid is a sudden incursion or attack

explanation.surface: A zealous baron joins an invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means extreme or fanatical in views, from the frenzy of the disease rabies.

clue.text: Up North catch son with drink

parts.note: to neck is slang for drinking quickly, gulping down

explanation.surface: In the north of England, a son catches a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up North' marks a dialect word of northern England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern dialect word for a door latch, a fastening or catch.

clue.text: Deeply impress English party

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: An English party leaves a lasting impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to fix firmly in the mind, a figurative sense of cutting into a surface.

clue.text: Because Rome's relinquished Old Master it must be genuine

parts.note: since can mean because

indicators.note: relinquished means given up, so two letters leave the city name

parts.note: the city's name; the 's here means 'has'
OM stands for Order of Merit, but read here as the initials of Old Master

explanation.surface: An art buyer reasons that the painting must be authentic because Rome has given up an Old Master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relinquished' removes O and M from ROME to leave RE; 'Rome's' reads as 'Rome has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine, free from pretence or deceit.

clue.text: List of goods in report

parts.note: to voice something is to express or report it

explanation.surface: A list of goods is included in the report.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill itemising goods supplied and their prices is a trade document listing them.

clue.text: See! Goitre can produce dizziness

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: the swollen-gland word can be made into something new by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Look! A goitre, a swollen neck gland, can make you dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See!' looks like an exclamation but is the Latin vide, abbreviated V; 'can produce' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a sensation of whirling and loss of balance, a medical name for dizziness.

clue.text: Building could become deficient after National Trust quits

indicators.note: could become says the remaining letters can be turned into another word
quits means leaves, so two letters depart from the fodder

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A historic building could fall into disrepair once the National Trust, Britain's heritage charity, pulls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' removes N and T from DEFICIENT, and 'could become' rearranges DEFICIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing building.

clue.text: Former husband crept about in passage

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: about means around in disorder, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: An ex-husband creeps around in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the rearrangement. 'passage' looks like a corridor but is a piece of text.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract quoted from a book or piece of music is a passage.

clue.text: They say I used to be hard. Nonsense!

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are as heard rather than as written

parts.note: I used to be means I was, in the past tense
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone claims they used to be tough, and the listener scoffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' gives the sound of 'I was', spelt EYE WAS, then H follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for rubbish or humbug, so it works as a dismissive exclamation like nonsense.

clue.text: What delight to be transported by river

parts.note: rapt means carried away with emotion, transported
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: What a joy to be carried along by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is intense joy or ecstasy, a strong form of delight.

clue.text: Distinctive character of ancient city hidden amongst volcanic rock

indicators.note: the old city is concealed among the rock, so its letters sit inside the lava word

parts.note: aa is a rough, clinkery kind of lava
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city buried in lava has a distinctive feel.
explanation.walkthrough: AA is a Hawaiian word for rough lava. 'hidden amongst' is a container here, not a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the distinctive atmosphere or quality that surrounds a person or place.

clue.text: Deliver Queen's additional clause

parts.note: to rid is to free or deliver from something
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal statement is delivered with an extra clause.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an amendment or extra provision added to a document or bill.

clue.text: Knocks back pole

indicators.note: back says the knocks word is turned to read the other way

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks

explanation.surface: Someone knocks back a pole, perhaps a drink with a Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole, as used for a ship's mast or boom.

clue.text: In short, engine part's source of energy

definitions.meaning: a shortened name for the carburettor, which mixes fuel and air in an engine
a shortened name for carbohydrate, a dietary fuel

explanation.surface: A car part supplies power, put briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' applies to both senses: each is an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are clipped forms: of carburettor, and of carbohydrate, which the body burns for fuel.

clue.text: Repeat section of Arne chorale

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A choir repeats a section of a chorale by the English composer Thomas Arne.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound or phrase that is repeated, so a repeat matches it.

clue.text: Mari and I go out to see Japanese art

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Mari and I go out to see some Japanese art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MARI, I and GO; 'go out' reads as a phrase but only 'out' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Value of a constant number

parts.note: C is the mathematical symbol for a constant
a count is a number or tally

explanation.surface: A mathematical constant's value.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to value it; account means worth or importance, as in 'of no account'.

clue.text: Expert fixers rebuilt the old stores investing foreign money mostly

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so the anagram wraps round the currency
rebuilt says the letters are put together again in a different order
mostly means the currency name loses its last letter

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: Skilled repairers rebuilt the old shops with foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' signals the anagram, 'mostly' drops the currency's last letter, and 'investing' means the anagram is wrapped round it, like clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: These people trace and solve faults or problems, so they are skilled fixers.
